Scatter at fixed true mass is smallest, sigma(b) about 0.1, at M500c ~ 1e14 Msun. At fixed true mass, HSE masses rise with z for groups and fall with z for clusters, and the scatter grows. X-COP (Eckert et al. 2018, arXiv:1805.00034), 13 nearby clusters with XMM+Planck: median non-thermal pressure fraction ~6% at R500 and ~10% at R200. This is lower than hydrodynamical simulations predict. With the Planck mass calibration, the gas fractions imply 1-b = 0.85 +/- 0.05 for SZ masses, with some evidence for a mass-dependent bias.

Nelson, Lau & Nagai 2014 (arXiv:1404.4636): the non-thermal pressure fraction profile is universal across redshift when radii are scaled to the mean matter density (R200m), not to the critical density. It depends strongly on mass accretion rate, and the non-thermal pressure is mainly radial. A fitting formula for f_nth(r/R200m) is given; parameter values are not yet extracted.

Simba (Sorini et al. 2024, arXiv:2409.05815), six feedback variants, 1e11 < M200c < 1e14 Msun, 0 < z < 4: gas-density profiles follow a power law. At fixed halo mass, slope and amplitude depend only weakly on redshift. With AGN jets on, haloes above M200c ~ 1e13 Msun have shallower (gentler) density profiles. A universal fitting formula for slope(M, z) and amplitude(M, z) is provided.

Barranco-Llorca et al. 2025 (arXiv:2511.10730), AMR cluster mergers at 0 <= z <= 1.5: at z=0 the HSE bias correlates only mildly with dynamical state. During a major merger the bias dips sharply negative around the merger time, then shows a transient positive peak, then slowly returns to its pre-merger level. This is driven mainly by changes in the gas-density morphology and dynamics, not by thermodynamics, and it shows weak dependence on mass ratio and impact parameter.
